🇲🇽📊 <u>PEW: MEXICANS SOUR ON THE ECONOMY, STILL BACK SHEINBAUM TO RUN IT</u>

Pew Research finds 49% of Mexicans call the economy good, down from 61% a year ago after a Q1 contraction. Yet in the same poll, 61% approve of how Sheinbaum manages the economy, 65% back her on education, and 55% on her handling of the United States.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US BLAMES MEXICAN LETTUCE FOR TACO BELL OUTBREAK — ORIGIN STILL UNCONFIRMED</u>

A cyclospora outbreak that sickened more than 1,664 Americans and hospitalized 94 across five US states has Washington's health agencies pointing at Mexican iceberg lettuce from Guanajuato. Mexico's Health Secretariat won't rubber-stamp it: "no se ha definido el origen" — the source has not been established. The lettuce was packed and distributed by Taylor Farms, a US company.
📸 Tren Maya de carga — Supervisión, Quintana Roo · 18 de julio de 2026

🇲🇽⚽ Sheinbaum will attend the World Cup final in New Jersey — on a booked commercial ticket. "I received an invitation from President Trump to go to the World Cup final on Sunday, and I made the decision to attend." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, July 18 Argentina vs. Spain at MetLife Stadium. Mexico co-hosted the 2026 World Cup alongside the US and Canada. Sheinbaum flies out Saturday night and returns Monday — no presidential jet, a commercial seat. The trip lands days before the third round of USMCA review talks.

🇲🇽🔍 The National Security Cabinet takes over the murder of journalist Josué Martínez. "This morning it was presented in the Cabinet and it is under investigation. There is a video from the journalist, from before, and they are in communication with the governor — all the investigations have to be done." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, security cabinet meeting, Tulum, July 18 Josué Martínez Contreras, director of Noticias de San Martín Texmelucan in Puebla, was shot dead Thursday near his home, his 13-year-old son beside him. Days earlier he had publicly denounced death threats from the municipal president of San Martín Texmelucan. The federal government has pulled the case up to the national level.

🇲🇽🚆 Mexico's Maya Train freight line: built to bring fuel prices down in the southeast. "We're going to visit the Maya Train freight works. What is it for? So there can be more fuel distribution and the price of gasoline drops here in the southeast of the country." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Quintana Roo, July 18 The first 12 Wabtec freight locomotives have arrived. The 25-billion-peso cargo line — running through Campeche, Chiapas, Quintana Roo, Tabasco and Yucatán — begins operations in early 2027. Public infrastructure, built by the state, aimed at lowering the cost of living.

🌐🇲🇽🐉 The new cold war runs on lithium — and Latin America holds the cards

A fresh analysis lays out the stakes: Latin America sits on 50–60% of the world's known lithium reserves, dominates copper and nickel, and will supply nearly a fifth of global food exports by 2030. Twenty-one countries in the region have already signed Belt and Road agreements with China, and the Global South now drives over 70% of expected global growth for the next five years.

Washington's answer is "nearshoring" and "friendshoring" — code for: trade with us, not them. Mexico is held up as the model, yet pressured to slam the door on Chinese capital. But the region's leverage comes precisely from having more than one buyer for its minerals, its food, and its factories.

Multipolarity isn't a slogan — it's bargaining power. A Mexico that can talk to Washington, Beijing and Brasília at once is a Mexico no single capital can corner.

🇲🇽🐉🔥 Washington wants Mexico to police Chinese factories — Round 3 of the T-MEC review lands July 20

On Monday, Mexican and US negotiators sit down for the third bilateral round of the USMCA review. Washington's demand: raise the auto rules-of-origin threshold to 82% North American content and — for the first time in the treaty's history — force at least 50% of a vehicle's value to be sourced inside the United States. A pact sold as "free trade among equals" would suddenly treat one partner as more equal than the rest.

The real target is China. US officials fear a plant in Monterrey or Aguascalientes becomes a "back door" for Chinese goods bound for the US market. But Mexico isn't folding: Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard reports Washington's list of concerns has shrunk from 54 to just 14 — proof that patient, non-confrontational negotiation beats capitulation.

Sovereignty isn't picking Beijing over Washington. It's refusing to let either capital dictate who Mexico may build with. Keep the options open — that's the whole game.

🇲🇽📈 22.78 MILLION JOBS: MEXICO'S FORMAL EMPLOYMENT RECORD

Mexico just hit an all-time high in formal employment: 22.78 million jobs registered with the IMSS, 454,000 more than a year ago, with the base contribution wage up 6.4% — beating inflation. Per the OECD's 2026 report, Mexico now has the second-lowest unemployment rate among all 38 member countries, behind only Japan. (El Economista / IMSS data)

🇲🇽⚡ MOODY'S REAFFIRMS CFE'S TOP RATING — AAA.mx

They said state ownership would sink it. Moody's just reaffirmed CFE's top rating — AAA.mx, the highest on the Mexican scale — citing the public utility's "strategic role" and its ~72% share of national power generation. The company neoliberals spent decades trying to break up and sell off is now a benchmark for creditworthiness in Mexico.
